flags.rationale: ENABLE_SHADOW_PREVIEW is the primary live flag. It is parsed in load_preview_env, sets shadow_enabled and effective_mode, and the runtime branch in preview_runtime_branch checks config.shadow_enabled to return the shadow_preview_path. The dedicated test confirms the end-to-end path from env var through parser to runtime branch.

ENABLE_PREVIEW_V2 is a live alias of ENABLE_SHADOW_PREVIEW. The parser accepts it and normalizes it to the same shadow_enabled=True and shadow path. It has no independent runtime branch. The test confirms it maps to the shadow path, and the runbook explicitly states it is not a standalone runtime branch.

PREVIEW_FORCE_LEGACY is dead at runtime. The parser records force_legacy_seen=True but preview_runtime_branch never checks it. The branch decision depends solely on shadow_enabled. The test explicitly asserts the branch remains legacy_preview_path when this flag is set, and legacy_force_label is a reporting-only helper. The runbook confirms the live service does not branch on it anymore.

summary.note: Three flags analyzed: ENABLE_SHADOW_PREVIEW is the sole live runtime branch controlling preview routing. ENABLE_PREVIEW_V2 is a legacy alias normalizing to the same path. PREVIEW_FORCE_LEGACY is dead at runtime with parser present but no branching.

cleanup_plan.rationale: Primary live flag controlling the preview runtime branch. No cleanup needed.

blockers: legacy deploy manifests may still reference ENABLE_PREVIEW_V2
cleanup_plan.rationale: Alias only. Normalize all deploy manifests to ENABLE_SHADOW_PREVIEW, then remove the elif branch in load_preview_env.

blockers: operator notes and reporting dashboards may still display force_legacy_seen in build_preview_plan output
cleanup_plan.rationale: Parser branch and legacy_force_label are reporting-only. Remove from config parsing once operator dashboards are updated, and clean up legacy.py.
